newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy union official -- room for early welfare talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy union official -- room for early welfare talks.

text.p: A senior Italian trades unionist said on Thursday that the labour movement might agree to bring forward to this year discussions with the government on reforms to welfare spending if a forthcoming mini-budget for 1997 leaves pensions and health spending untouched.
The remarks by Guglielmo Epifani, number two in the main CGIL labour confederation, were welcomed by deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni. "What he has said is important," Veltroni said.

Italy's trades unions have until now bitterly opposed calls by Prime Minister Romano Prodi to bring forward a planned review of pensions spending and other welfare provisions in 1998 forward by one year.
Epifani made his compromise proposal of no cuts now for talks ahead of schedule at a debate organised by the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the biggest force in Prodi's coalition.
He later told Reuters: "If the government touches pensions and health (in the mini-budget) it will become impossible for us to talk about a reform of the welfare state afterwards.

"If, however, this mini-budget does not touch health spending or, directly or indirectly, pensions spending, it will be easier to have talks with the government, unions and parliament on reform of the welfare state in a short time."
